title: It Sure Looks Like the Department of Education Is Promoting a Right-Wing ‘Harry Potter’ Meme
gist: The US Department of Education posted a Hogwarts-style image with 'Make Education Great Again' that online observers read as adopting the far-right 'Malfoid' fan-fiction meme; Wired argues this reflects government communications absorbing toxic internet subcultures as political signaling.

insights.claim: The 'Malfoid' meme, a gender-flipped female Draco Malfoy, originated on fan-fiction sites like Archive of Our Own and was turned into a far-right aesthetic that romanticizes blood-purity bigotry.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Shows how niche fandom content is repurposed as extremist branding that spreads via meme channels and Telegram.
insights.locator: The Malfoid concept did not come from conservative think tanks

insights.claim: The term Malfoid combines Malfoy with the incel slur 'foid', and the character is depicted as anti-queer and anti-trans, serving as a mascot for ethno-nationalism packaged in a shareable pop-culture aesthetic.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Aesthetic packaging lowers the barrier to radicalization compared with traditional propaganda.
insights.locator: The term Malfoid is a portmanteau

insights.claim: The Department of Education's October 27 X post ('There's Magic in Learning!', 'Make Education Great Again') was read by online commentators as embracing the Malfoid meme, and the department kept posting Lord of the Rings and Avatar references afterward.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Federal agencies are now treated as participants in meme culture, creating reputational and platform-attention risk.
insights.locator: At first glance, the Department of Education's October 27 X post

insights.claim: The Trump administration has normalized meme communication, with Trump's Truth Social feed full of AI-generated meme imagery and agencies like DHS using memes and Tolkien material about ICE raids.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Expect continued use of AI-generated imagery in official channels, increasing demand for synthetic-media moderation and attribution.
insights.locator: Similarly, the Trump administration has normalized communicating

insights.claim: Prominent right-wing figures such as Peter Thiel and Elon Musk have long co-opted The Lord of the Rings for political ends.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Fantasy franchises are recurrent vehicles for tech-right ideology.
insights.locator: Prominent right-wingers using fantasy and fiction

insights.claim: Baylor communications professor Leslie Hahner argues the collapse of boundaries between internet subcultures and mainstream institutions is a defining feature of modern politics, and that either ignorance or intent behind the post would be significant.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Frames the post as either a competence failure or deliberate signaling, both politically meaningful.
insights.quote: Is the agency unaware of the symbol’s cultural baggage, or does it believe these associations are useful for attracting engagement from relevant audiences?
insights.locator: Leslie Hahner, a communications professor at Baylor

insights.claim: The Department of Education answered Wired's request for comment only with a Dumbledore quote, declining to address the meme directly.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Non-denial responses keep the ambiguity that fuels engagement.
insights.locator: In response to WIRED's request for comment

insights.claim: The author argues political persuasion is shifting from policy papers to aesthetic identity, because young voters trained on TikTok and Wattpad consume information through hyper-specific tropes rather than cohesive ideologies.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Campaigns and platforms that master trope-driven content gain an advantage with young voters.
insights.quote: Policy papers, detailed legislative agendas, and traditional campaign speeches simply do not enthuse the youth anymore; aesthetic identity does.
insights.locator: We are witnessing the end of traditional political persuasion

insights.claim: Coded imagery works as an 'algorithmic wink' that signals alignment to extreme online constituencies without triggering traditional media oversight.
insights.speaker: Michaela Makusha
insights.so_what: Dog-whistle visuals evade moderation and press scrutiny, a persistent trust-and-safety gap.
insights.locator: By utilizing the visual markers of the Malfoid
